court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Surendra S/O Manoharrao Bhele vs Latika W/O Surendra Bhele And Others

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Shri Surendra s/o Manoharrao Bhele, husband
parties.respondent_defendant: Latika w/o Surendra Bhele, wife, and minor sons Arpit @ Bikin and Sanket

facts_of_case: The petitioner is challenging a judgment allowing an application under Section 127 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The marriage was solemnized in 1997, but the husband developed a drinking habit and started pressurizing his wife to bring Rs.50,000/- from her father. She refused and was subjected to cruelty.

legal_principles.principle: A spouse who is able to maintain their family but willfully neglects them may be ordered to pay maintenance.
legal_principles.held: It was also a finding of fact, which was recorded by learned Magistrate, that husband has willfully neglected wife and sons and is willfully not maintaining them in spite of the fact that he is able to maintain them.
use_in: divorce cases where one spouse is not supporting the other

legal_principles.principle: A court may consider a spouse's previous maintenance arrangements when determining their current maintenance needs.
legal_principles.held: It was stated in the application that while considering application under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, learned Magistrate also considered maintenance, which wife used to get in Hindu marriage petition under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
use_in: cases where a spouse's previous maintenance arrangements are relevant to their current situation

outcome.final_order: The writ petition is finally heard by consent of the parties and is dismissed.
